name: Arapaho

reviewScope.method: Read both complete packets, recomputed all proposed public annotation/scope/subscope/claim budgets, and independently spotchecked actual saved primary texts. Reopened the three existing supporting original routes and the existing article landing page for metadata checks; no new source discovery, Site/canonical edits, contact or delegation.
reviewScope.notClaimed: Not a full canonical-profile audit, whole-book/code reading, fresh review of underlying research data, legal assessment or media-rights clearance. No original interviews, tapes, photographs or story transcripts accessed or reused.

northern.result: Matches packet. Original p18-s2/p18-s3 navigation URLs preserved as supporting renewals; selected code collection counts once, and Arthur/Porter counts once.

history.result: Matches packet. Original NPS home route retained visibly; canonical www.nps.gov route actually read. Brief Stories page remains supporting. Foundation and Roberts article are distinct substantial works.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Existing Northern Arapaho homepage reopened directly. Actual institutional navigation lines 0–36 and Wind River location statement 39–41 read.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS: narrow institutional starting-point claim fits. No acreage, population, offices, service outcomes, social posts or video adopted. Supporting count is appropriate.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Packet and author's precise original-inspection record reviewed. Independent reopening of the exact query-string department URL timed out in this audit.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS WITH ACCESS LIMIT: recorded directory/short-description scope and conservative supporting status are internally appropriate. This audit does not claim a second actual directory-body inspection. The new timeout does not negate the author's earlier documented actual reading or justify a substantive count.
independentEvidenceChecks.accessLimit: No additional retries, replacement search snippets or access-control workarounds.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Saved education-code.pdf verified as 31 pages. Actual selected page 2 section 102, pages 5–6 section 104(c), and page 31 history note read. Complete saved two-page code-preface.pdf also read.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS: educational self-determination, Arapaho language/history, academic learning, parental/community participation, and explicit Eastern Shoshone disclaimer are supported. Enactment is May 4, 2006, Resolution 2006-9070, not the 2026 upload path. Preface excludes regulations and specified internal-government resolutions and distinguishes commentary from enactments. Legislation is correctly treated as dated policy, without present-law or implementation guarantees.
independentEvidenceChecks.counting: One selected code collection includes title, preface and index; none adds an independent source count.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Saved arthur-porter-2019.pdf verified as 16 pages. Actual printed 69–73 and 80–81 (PDF 1–5, 12–13) read. Existing original journal landing also reopened; authors, online date, issue and CC BY 4.0 statement read.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS: Arthur explicitly identifies himself as a Northern Arapaho tribal member; attribution is not inferred from employment. Authorship/positionality and interviews, talking circles, observation, autoethnography and historical work are actual methods. The paper is a situated 2019 interpretation, not a representative survey, tribal government statement, current prevalence study or clinical-results publication.
independentEvidenceChecks.scopeChecks: Shared Wind River projects do not erase Eastern Shoshone/Northern Arapaho distinctions. Shoshone bison/gathering initiatives are not relabeled Arapaho. The broader first-person 'we' and population/health estimates are not generalized in the packet. No creation narrative, prophecy, participant quote or figure is republished.
independentEvidenceChecks.datesAndRights: Print imprint is Volume 9 Supplement 2 / Fall 2019, pages 69–84; online publication November 11, 2019 matches publisher. Current landing labels the issue 9(B) and explicitly identifies author copyright and CC BY 4.0. No source media reused.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Canonical existing www.nps.gov Stories page reopened. Actual public body lines 22–30 and last-updated line 33 read.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS: descendant/family accounts and archival investigation are actual content. April 24, 2025 is a displayed update rather than a proven first-publication date. The brief page is supporting; linked letters, testimony, imagery and casualty counts do not enter the proposed synthesis. Retained home.nps.gov route is clearly described as an access route, not a second work.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Saved sand-foundation-2017.pdf verified as 62 pages. Cover, actual printed introduction 2 (PDF 6), and printed 28–29 (PDF 32–33) read.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS: cover establishes December 2017; introduction identifies a foundation for planning/management. Printed 28 states tribal histories inform interpretation and identifies further youth/oral-history opportunities. Printed 29 lists tribal vetting and revision of draft research and further review/input as needs. The proposed claim correctly presents dated institutional priorities, without implying that planned or proposed work was completed.
independentEvidenceChecks.limits: No sensitive site description, artifact/survey location, ceremonial detail, casualty total, record collection, map or source image is reproduced. Planning document does not establish one universal Arapaho position or current arrangements.

independentEvidenceChecks.actualInspection: Saved crm-v23n9.pdf verified as 56 pages. Issue cover and complete actual Alexa Roberts article on printed/PDF 43–46 read.
independentEvidenceChecks.result: PASS: cover establishes CRM 23(9), 2000; article byline and concluding author note identify Roberts and her NPS project role. Printed 43 explains sensitive intellectual-property concerns. Printed 44 explicitly describes the Northern Arapaho Tribe conducting its own project beginning April 1999 under a cooperative agreement. Printed 44–46 describe different Cheyenne arrangements. The claim does not merge those projects or reproduce their content.
independentEvidenceChecks.rightsScope: Permissions described for the original NPS report and archives do not establish Atlas permission to reuse tapes, transcripts or photographs. Packet correctly supplies only a public methodological summary and explicitly disclaims original-recording/media access. One article is one work; entire issue, individual interviews, bibliography and mirror add no counts.
independentEvidenceChecks.accessProvenance: Independent archive mirror is transparently named in source metadata. This audit read the saved actual article, without independently rechecking every archival-link redirect or asserting the mirror is an NPS-owned domain.

wordBudgetCheck.method: Whitespace-separated words in each source annotation + full contentReviewScope + every inspected-subresource scope + all supplied cited claim blocks. Final column adds rightsNote. No proposed overview. Citation locators/private evidence notes and metadata are not proposed public synthesis. Recompute if legacy body or overview is retained at integration.

integrationReminders: Use the four substantive works plus three honest supporting cards without elevating directories, brief Stories, indexes or subresources to meet a target.
Keep Northern Arapaho, Eastern Shoshone and Southern Arapaho peoples and governments distinct; a shared reservation, research project or public institution does not make one political body.

Keep 2006 policy, 2017 planning and 2019 research explicitly dated. Planned research, policy aspirations and observed participant experiences do not establish completed programs, current law or clinical effects.
Replace overlapping baseline text rather than append duplicate prose. Packet word budgets do not authorize additional legacy sections or a newly cited overview without a fresh combined count.

Original photographs, interviews, audio, transcripts and oral narratives remain outside the Atlas synthesis and asset permissions. No source discovery or further corrective research is required by this bounded audit.
